name: 3D and advanced specimen imaging
description: 3D models, photogrammetry, X-ray and spectral imaging of specimens, and the data these produce.

name: Access and benefit sharing
description: Access and benefit-sharing, digital sequence information, permits and compliance, and preventing biopiracy.
aliases: data provenance and value return to primary data collectors

name: Aeroecology and animal migration
description: Monitoring and forecasting animal movement and migration through the air using weather radar, telemetry and related data.

name: Agricultural biodiversity and pest management
description: Biodiversity data for agriculture: crop genetic resources, pests and natural enemies, precision and robotic pest control.

name: AI agents and conversational data access
description: LLM agents, MCP servers, chatbots and question-answering systems that let people or machines query and analyse biodiversity data conversationally.
aliases: AI agents for scientific data analysis
AI assistants for data publishing support
LLM agent access to biodiversity data

name: AI crawlers and bot traffic
description: The load and cost that AI crawlers and bots place on biodiversity data services, and responses such as rate limiting and cost recovery.

name: AI-assisted digitisation
description: Computer vision and machine learning applied to specimen images and digitisation workflows: segmentation, landmarking, measurement, clustering and other automated processing of digitised collections.

name: AI-assisted software development
description: Using LLMs and coding agents to build, document and prototype biodiversity software.

name: AI-assisted species identification
description: Machine-learning models that identify or classify organisms from images, sound or other signals, and how their outputs are combined with human expertise.

name: AI-ready data
description: Making biodiversity data and metadata fit for machine learning: readiness definitions and metrics, dataset documentation (e.g. Croissant, dataset cards) and FAIR-for-AI.
aliases: AI-ready and FAIR for AI data

name: Automated sensor-based monitoring
description: High-throughput biodiversity monitoring with automated sensors (light traps, cameras, acoustic devices and multimodal sensor networks) and the pipelines that turn detections into data.

name: Bioacoustics and passive acoustic monitoring
description: Recording, analysing and standardising animal sounds and soundscapes, including AI sound classifiers.

name: Biobanks, seed banks and living collections
description: Tissue and genetic-resource biobanks, seed banks and living collections, and tracking samples through them.

name: Biodiversity digital twins
description: Building and operationalising digital twins of ecosystems, sensor systems and the ocean, and assessing their maturity.

name: Biodiversity indicators and policy reporting
description: Indicators, Essential Biodiversity Variables, data cubes and assessments that connect biodiversity data to policy (e.g. KMGBF, IPBES, Red List).

name: Biodiversity literature mining
description: Extracting occurrences, traits, names and other data from biodiversity literature and grey literature with text mining and NLP.

name: Camera trap data
description: Managing, processing, standardising (e.g. Camtrap DP) and publishing camera-trap imagery and detections.
aliases: AI pipeline for images and video

name: Capacity building and workforce
description: Training, certification, curricula and retaining skilled people in biodiversity informatics and collections.

name: Citizen science
description: Community and volunteer observation platforms, their data, identification behaviour, verification and integration into research.

name: Collection and data use and impact
description: Tracking how collections and published data are used (loans, citations, downloads) and demonstrating their impact and return on investment.

name: Collection data models
description: Modelling collection objects and events: material entities, lots, storage units, transactions, movements and collection state.

name: Collection descriptions and registries
description: Describing collections at collection level (e.g. Latimer Core), collection registries, and making undigitised or hidden collections discoverable.

name: Collection management systems
description: Software for managing collection data (e.g. Specify, Symbiota and institutional systems): data models, migration, replacement, hosting and publishing.

name: Colonial legacies and decolonisation
description: Colonial provenance of collections and data, decolonisation and repatriation of data.

name: Community engagement and outreach
description: Engaging stakeholders, communities and the public: communication, outreach, collaboration and participation.

name: Conservation and restoration practice
description: Applying biodiversity data to species conservation, protected areas and ecosystem restoration, including community-led conservation.

name: Controlled vocabularies
description: Building, governing and aligning controlled vocabularies, thesauri and term lists (including multilingual ones).

name: Critical perspectives on AI
description: Grounded, sceptical framings of what machine learning and LLMs actually do, separating capability from hype and considering AI's effect on knowledge creation.

name: Darwin Core Data Package
description: The Darwin Core Data Package (DwC-DP) and conceptual model: design, profiles, adoption, and transition from Darwin Core Archives and ABCD.
aliases: ABCD to Darwin Core Data Package transition
agent roles in Darwin Core Data Package

name: Darwin Core mapping and crosswalks
description: Mapping and transforming source data to Darwin Core and other schemas, crosswalks, templates and tools that help data holders standardise.

name: Data access control and licensing
description: Licences, embargoes, data agreements, access rights and machine-actionable policies governing data use.

name: Data and digital sovereignty
description: Who controls biodiversity data and infrastructure, at national, institutional and community level.

name: Data discovery and search
description: Finding biodiversity data and resources: discoverability, federated search and indexing.

name: Data gaps and biases
description: Taxonomic, geographic and temporal gaps and biases in biodiversity data and the knowledge shortfalls they create.

name: Data governance and stewardship
description: Institutional and community governance and stewardship of biodiversity data.

name: Data packaging and exchange formats
description: Formats for packaging and exchanging datasets, such as Frictionless data packages, RO-Crate and self-describing files.

name: Data preservation and storage
description: Long-term preservation, archiving and storage of biodiversity data at scale.

name: Data provenance
description: Recording where data came from and how they were processed, including versioning, paradata and auditability.

name: Data publishing and mobilisation
description: Getting data from holders into aggregators such as GBIF: publishing pipelines, ingestion, continuous and automated publication, and barriers to publishing.

name: Data quality assessment
description: Tests, flags, validation and cleaning that assess and improve the quality of biodiversity records (e.g. BDQ tests).

name: Data rescue and historical data
description: Rescuing at-risk and historical biodiversity data and using it to establish baselines.

name: Data round-tripping and provider feedback
description: Returning annotations, corrections and quality feedback from aggregators and users to data providers and closing the loop.

name: Data timeliness and latency
description: The lag between observation, identification and data becoming available for action.

name: Data visualisation
description: Visualising biodiversity data and taxonomies with interactive and open-source tools.

name: Decision support and dashboards
description: Tools, dashboards and alerting systems that turn biodiversity data into information for managers and decision-makers.

name: Digital extended specimen
description: Linking specimens to derived data, samples, sequences, media, archives and other specimens so the specimen record becomes a connected network.

name: Digitisation planning and prioritisation
description: Deciding what to digitise and to what level: prioritisation, backlogs, frameworks, monitoring progress and digitisation on demand.

name: Drone-based monitoring
description: Using drones and aerial video for wildlife and behaviour monitoring, including detection and tracking of individuals.

name: Environmental and compute costs of AI
description: Energy use, carbon footprint and compute cost of AI and IT, and frugal or green approaches to reduce them.

name: Environmental DNA
description: eDNA, metabarcoding, environmental genomics and ancient DNA as sources of biodiversity occurrence data.

name: Evidence synthesis and actionable knowledge
description: Synthesising evidence from data and literature into actionable knowledge for research and decision-making.

name: Extending data standards
description: Designing and adopting extensions to Darwin Core and related standards for new data types.

name: FAIR data principles
description: Applying, evaluating and critiquing the FAIR principles for biodiversity data, collections and workflows.

name: FAIR digital objects
description: Packaging data as FAIR Digital Objects with persistent, machine-actionable identifiers and typed metadata, and related signposting.

name: Fitness for use
description: Judging whether data are fit for a particular purpose: use cases, task-specific quality and the context of use.

name: Foundation models and imageomics
description: Large pretrained vision, language and geospatial models for organismal biology, and imageomics as a field extracting biological traits from images.

name: Freshwater biodiversity data
description: Freshwater species, habitats and river systems: data platforms, taxonomy, spatial units and assessment under the Water Framework Directive.

name: Funding models for biodiversity infrastructure
description: How infrastructures and data work are funded: funding models, diversification, costs, valuation and the effects of funding cuts.

name: Geographic standards and gazetteers
description: Gazetteers, higher geography, administrative and natural boundaries and geographic schemes (e.g. WGSRPD) used to describe where biodiversity occurs.

name: Georeferencing
description: Assigning coordinates and uncertainty to locality descriptions, including legacy and historical localities.

name: Geoscience and mineral collections
description: Geological and mineral collections data, geologic context, stratigraphy and their place in TDWG standards.

name: Geospatial data infrastructure
description: Cloud-native geospatial formats, catalogues (e.g. STAC), web GIS and reproducible geospatial pipelines for biodiversity data.

name: Habitat classification
description: Classifying habitats and ecosystem types (e.g. EUNIS) and the characteristic species that define them.

name: Historical archives and field notes
description: Field notes, correspondence, illustrations, expedition records and institutional archives as sources of biodiversity data and context.

name: Human-in-the-loop validation
description: Workflows in which experts or volunteers review, correct and validate automated or AI outputs.

name: Identification keys and descriptive data
description: Interactive and multi-access identification keys, structured descriptive data (e.g. SDD) and character matrices, including hybrids with AI.

name: Identification provenance and uncertainty
description: Recording who or what identified an organism, how confident the identification is, and how human and machine identifications are exchanged.

name: Identifying and crediting people
description: Disambiguating collectors, determiners and other agents, person identifiers, and attribution and credit for data work.

name: Indigenous data governance
description: Indigenous data sovereignty and governance, the CARE principles, Local Contexts labels, and Indigenous perspectives on biodiversity data.

name: Infrastructure resilience and risk
description: Resilience of research infrastructures to cyber attacks, funding shocks, geopolitical, energy and climate risks, and designs that reduce fragility.

name: Infrastructure sustainability
description: Keeping biodiversity data infrastructures, repositories, tools and APIs going over time, including succession and decommissioning.

name: Invasive species
description: Detecting, mapping and managing invasive alien species and supporting regulation with data.

name: Knowledge graphs
description: Constructing and using RDF and property-graph knowledge graphs to connect biodiversity data, literature and knowledge.

name: Knowledge representation and meaning
description: Representing scientific statements, causal knowledge and context so meaning survives reuse (e.g. semantic units, Rosetta statements).

name: Label transcription and OCR
description: Transcribing specimen labels, cards, handwritten records and printed text with OCR, handwriting recognition and multimodal LLMs, and evaluating transcription quality.
aliases: structured data extraction from collection records

name: Legacy data migration
description: Moving and cleaning legacy databases, images and records into new systems and formats.

name: Legacy literature digitisation
description: Digitising and providing access to historical biodiversity literature (e.g. the Biodiversity Heritage Library), its interfaces, partnerships and sustainability.

name: Linked open data and Wikidata
description: Publishing and linking biodiversity entities as linked open data, notably in Wikidata.

name: LLM evaluation and hallucination
description: Measuring the accuracy, uncertainty and cost of LLM outputs, and detecting or controlling hallucination.
aliases: large language models as next-token predictors

name: LLM-based information extraction
description: Using large language models to extract, structure and enrich biodiversity information from text and records, including prompt and schema design.

name: Local and edge AI
description: Running AI models on local machines, on-device or at the edge (in the field or in museums) rather than via cloud services.

name: Long-term and national monitoring
description: Long-term ecological research, national and regional monitoring networks and protected-area monitoring programmes.
aliases: national biodiversity monitoring in Saudi Arabia

name: Marine biodiversity data
description: Marine species and ocean data, marine geographic units and gazetteers, and land-sea integration.

name: Minimum information standards for digitisation
description: Defining minimum or complete information levels for digitised specimens (e.g. MIDS) and measuring data completeness.

name: ML training data and benchmarks
description: Building, sharing and evaluating training datasets and benchmarks for biodiversity machine learning, including use of museum images as training data.
aliases: museum collection images as training data

name: Molecular and sequence data
description: DNA barcodes and sequence data: curation, metadata, provenance and linking to specimens.

name: Multilingual biodiversity data
description: Localisation, translation and multilingual access to biodiversity data and tools.

name: National and regional biodiversity data networks
description: GBIF nodes, national biodiversity information systems, hosted and regional portals, and national data strategies.

name: Ontologies
description: Developing, cataloguing, aligning and governing ontologies and semantic artefacts, and ontology-based data access and integration.

name: Open data and open science
description: Open data, open science and open access infrastructure, and pressures on openness (including from AI).

name: Palaeontology data
description: Fossil collections and palaeontological data, including deep-time environmental data.

name: Persistent identifiers
description: Persistent and content-based identifiers for specimens, samples, media, names, literature and organisms, and their stability.

name: Personal data and privacy
description: Protecting the privacy of collectors, observers and researchers in biodiversity data.

name: Provenance of AI-derived data
description: Recording which models, versions and processes produced AI-generated annotations and records so they can be traced, trusted and reproduced.

name: Remote sensing and Earth observation
description: Satellite, airborne and spectral data for mapping land cover, habitats and organisms, and integrating Earth observation with occurrence data.
aliases: harmonising occurrence and Earth observation data

name: Reproducible workflows
description: Reproducibility of analyses and workflow systems for executing and sharing them.

name: Research infrastructure landscape
description: How biodiversity research infrastructures fit together: scope, governance, federation, European data spaces and the visibility of infrastructure.

name: Research software architecture
description: Architectural choices for biodiversity software: APIs, microservices, event-driven and cloud-native systems.

name: Responsible and trustworthy AI
description: Governance, security, interpretability and trust in AI systems used by biodiversity institutions, and the risks AI poses.
aliases: AI governance in the public sector

name: Retrieval-augmented generation
description: Grounding language-model answers in retrieved documents or knowledge graphs (RAG, GraphRAG, vector and hybrid search).

name: Sampling-event and survey data
description: Structured survey and sampling-event data: protocols, sampling effort, absences, abundance and detectability (e.g. Humboldt Extension).

name: Schema design and data modelling
description: Designing typed schemas and data models (e.g. LinkML), schema validation and specification-driven data capture.

name: Semantic and FAIR publishing
description: Publishing taxonomic treatments and articles as structured, machine-readable, FAIR content and linking publications to data.

name: Semantic interoperability
description: Integrating heterogeneous data across domains and systems through shared semantics, annotation and harmonisation.

name: Sensitive and restricted-access species data
description: Protecting sensitive species locations: generalisation, restricted access, standards for withheld information, and the costs and harms of over-restriction.

name: Species distribution modelling
description: Modelling species distributions and ecological niches from occurrence and environmental data, and the data requirements this places on infrastructures.

name: Specimen and record annotation
description: Annotating specimen and occurrence records by people and machines (e.g. machine annotation services), and validating annotations.

name: Specimen digitisation
description: Digitising natural history specimens and collections, from imaging workflows and stations to national and legacy digitisation programmes.

name: Standards development and governance
description: How TDWG and other bodies develop, review, ratify, version and sustain standards, and how standards evolve and are adopted.

name: Taxon concepts and taxonomic change
description: Representing taxon concepts, taxonomic uncertainty and change over time, and identifiers for taxa.

name: Taxonomic backbones and checklists
description: Building, curating and publishing species checklists, national taxonomies and global taxonomic backbones (e.g. Catalogue of Life), and their relationship to one another.

name: Taxonomic expertise and the taxonomic impediment
description: The shortage and loss of taxonomic expertise, dark taxa, identification bottlenecks, and efforts to map, capture and grow taxonomic knowledge.

name: Taxonomic name matching
description: Parsing, matching and reconciling scientific names against reference lists, and handling synonyms, homonyms and verbatim names.

name: TDWG community and governance
description: TDWG as an organisation: governance, interest groups, membership, finances and conference formats.

name: Traditional knowledge and sociobiodiversity
description: Representing traditional knowledge and the social dimensions of biodiversity (sociobiodiversity) in data and standards.

name: Trait and phenology data
description: Functional, morphological and phenological trait data: measurement, units, extraction and FAIR publication.

name: Trust and research ethics
description: Trust between data holders, infrastructures and users, and ethical conduct in biodiversity research.

name: Type specimens
description: Inventorying, cataloguing and linking name-bearing type specimens.

name: Under-resourced and orphaned collections
description: Collections with little funding or staff, orphaned collections and low-barrier ways to mobilise their data.

name: Urban biodiversity
description: Biodiversity data and patterns in cities and along urbanisation gradients.

name: User-centred design
description: Designing tools and infrastructures around user needs, with requirements elicitation, co-design and agile methods.

name: Vector-borne disease surveillance
description: Medical entomology collections and data supporting surveillance of disease vectors.

name: Volunteer and community curation
description: Curation of data by volunteers and communities, and sustaining volunteer-run efforts.
